native/resume-token/current: Wire-level boundary placement during resume replay; no snapshot is raised before CURRENT. Production was consistent across the two runs (r1 nmuuicyas, r2 nmuukwo6n): ADD, boundary, documentChange b, boundary, CURRENT, boundary. fireemu strict sends the same frames without the boundary between the change and CURRENT. Native-gRPC client effect: a raw gRPC listener sees one boundary frame fewer than in production; an SDK listener cannot, because its target is not yet current. Issue fs-listen-resume-replay-boundaries.
native/existence-filter/with-expected-co: Wire-level boundary placement during resume replay; no snapshot is raised before CURRENT. Production was consistent across the two runs (r1 nmuuicyas, r2 nmuukwo6n): ADD, boundary, documentDelete b, boundary, documentChange c with removed target ids, boundary, CURRENT, boundary. fireemu strict sends the same two document messages with no boundary after each. Native-gRPC client effect: a raw gRPC listener sees two boundary frames fewer than in production (the document messages themselves match); an SDK listener cannot, because its target is not yet current. Issue fs-listen-resume-replay-boundaries.
native/existence-filter/without-expected: Production was consistent across the two runs once the optional existence filter is set aside (r1 nmuuicyas sent filter(1,1), r2 nmuukwo6n sent none): ADD, boundary, CURRENT, boundary, with no document message although a document was deleted and another left the query while no stream was open. fireemu strict sends the exact diff (documentChange c with removed target ids, documentDelete b). Native-gRPC client effect: a raw gRPC listener that gave no expected count receives two document messages that production does not send; the SDK always gives an expected count, which is the row above. Which answer production gives depends on its history window, which is not observable, so it is recorded, not fitted. Issue fs-listen-resume-replay-boundaries.
native/resume-token/invalid: Production removes a target whose token is not a token (INVALID_ARGUMENT, no ADD). The official emulator (firebase-tools 15.28.2) ignores the token, sends RESET and replays everything; the emulator profile must not refuse what the official emulator completes, so it keeps the RESET. Strict follows production (MATCH).
native/target-protocol/id-after-assigned: Production ends the stream (INVALID_ARGUMENT) when an explicit target id follows a server-assigned one. The official emulator accepts it (ADD[7]); the emulator profile accepts it too. Strict follows production (MATCH).
native/target-protocol/missing-index: Production removes a target whose query needs a composite index (ADD, then REMOVE with FAILED_PRECONDITION). The official emulator ignores index requirements and serves the query; the emulator profile has no index validation, so the target is served and the wait for REMOVE runs out. Strict follows production (MATCH).
